articleTitle: Haptic Exercises for Measuring Improvement of Post-Stroke Rehabilitation Patients
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: Rehabilitation exercises supervised by occupational therapists (OTs), involve applying task-oriented forces to the injured/disabled area to regain, for instance, strength and range of motion. Haptic interfaces have shown clear benefits in imitating therapists' exercises with the possibilities of position, grasping angles and force capturing. In this paper, we present two haptic-based virtual reality exercises for stroke patients undergoing rehabilitation to recover all, or some, of their lost hand functions. The two exercises, the squeeze ball exercise and the maze exercise, were implemented using the CyberForce system. The squeeze ball exercise helps patients recover the action of hand grasping whereas the maze exercise aims at increasing the steadiness of the patient's movement. Our measurements of these exercises show that we can continuously evaluate the patient's improvement.

articleTitle: Development of EMFI-sensor based pressure sensitive insole for gait analysis
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: The pressure distribution of the sole includes important information of gait during walking or running. For example, by monitoring the details of pressure distributions in the sole in normal walking many malpositions of the foot can be easily detected. In this study a simple and versatile EMFI sensor based real-time pressure mapping system was developed for gait analysis purposes. The system consists of a thin and flexible insole, including 16 tiny EMFI sensor elements, connected via a customized analog amplifier and digital data acquisition card to a PC computer. The PC-software of the measurement system shows the pressure in each small sensor element of the sole in real time, and records the data to a file. The accuracy and reliability of the system was preliminarily evaluated by experimental measurements. The results showed out that the system has capability to measure the pressure distributions of the foot sole reliably. The correlation coefficient between the applied pressure and the sensor output was 0,99. The next phase of the research project is to evaluate applicability of the system for evaluation of gait with large number of test subjects.

articleTitle: New Device for Assessment of Autonomous Nervous System Functioning in Psychophysiology
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: In the paper a new device for autonomic nervous system patterns assessment with application in psychophysiology is presented. The system is characterized by two physical sensing channels, expressed by skin conductance and ballistography (BCG), and a set of virtual sensing channels based on advanced processing of the physical channels information to obtain heart rate, respiratory signal, sympathetic flow to the heart and sweat glands, parasympathetic outflow to the heart and heart rate variability measurement. A low cost, small size acquisition multifunction input-output board is used to control the conditioning circuits and to acquire the voltage of the sensing channels. Referring to the software, an advanced processing block including digital filters, peak-detector and wavelet decomposition block was designed and implemented using LabVIEW. The system permits quantification of skin conductance variation and heart rate variability for different psychophysiological and pathological state.

articleTitle: Automatic Measurement of the Intima-Media Thickness with Active Contour Based Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: A snake-based approach for the automatic detection of the intima-media thickness (IMT) of the far wall of the common carotid artery from sonographic images is proposed. The main problems to be faced are related, from one point, to the high level of speckle noise and, from the other, to the need of an accurate segmentation of the vessel structure for diagnostic purposes. In particular, the detection of the intima layer plays a fundamental role as it represents the initial contour from where the method should start. We propose an automatic segmentation approach which makes use of a first non linear filtering based on anisotropic diffusion followed by an iterative relaxation procedure. Once the intima layer has been detected our method tries to locate an optimal initial contour to detect the wall of the artery by minimizing of a modified energy functional.

articleTitle: Surface Measurement of the Human Lymphocyte Micro-Nucleus in Image Affected by Alterations
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: In order to relieve structural chromosome aberrations, a new architecture of flow cytometer measurement device able to recognize and automatic count the Micro Nucleuses (MNs) on the acquired images of human lymphocytes has been pointed out. The technique adopted to perform the MN detection is based on the pattern matching algorithm. Biologist experts recommend that the correct detection of MN must respect the condition that the MN's surface is in the range off [1/3, 1/16] of the nucleus. The pattern matching algorithm can give only a coarse evaluation of the MN dimension. On the basis of these considerations, the paper proposes to cascade the pattern matching algorithm and the blob analysis in order to achieve the accurate evaluation of the MN surface. In order to evaluate the valid gray level used to threshold the image the pattern matching algorithm furnishes: (i) the coordinate (x, y) and (ii) the parameter about the coarse evaluation of MN dimension. So the blob analysis can be applied and the surfaces of both the MN and the nucleuses are accurately evaluated.

articleTitle: Processing EEG signals for Clinical Interpretation in Seizure-Suspected Patients
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: Epilepsy is one of the most common neurological disorders, affecting around 1 in 200 of the population. However, identifying epilepsy can be difficult because seizures tend to be relatively infrequent events and an electroencephalogram (EEG) does not always show abnormalities. The aim of this project is to develop a new methods that could improve the diagnosis of epilepsy, leading to earlier treatment and to a better quality of life for epileptic patients. The above methods must be composed with a flexible hardware development in order to discriminate noise and had signals from correct EEG, MEG (Magnetoencephalogram) and Eye Image recognition. Even if there are EEG signal classifiers, it is suitable to perform a correct signal processing according to particular clinical reference, that is, it is difficult to have a classifier for all circumstances but it is possible to adapt EEG processing on current patient. This paper deals with a new approach of developing an architecture with a an embedded coding included in a framework agreement between University and IRCCS "E. Medea".

articleTitle: Fetal Electrocardiogram Signal Modelling Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: The fetal electrocardiogram signal (FECG) is a major tool in monitoring and diagnosis of the fetus high risk conditions and arrhythmias. This paper introduces an accurate mathematical model for fetal electrocardiogram based on a real template FECG signal. This is done after elimination of maternal electrocardiogram (MECG) signal interference measured during pregnancy. The parameters of the introduced model are optimized in terms of sum square error using a genetic algorithm (GA). Our precise fetal electrocardiogram model can be a benchmark for other prospective researches particularly in FECG extraction

articleTitle: Signal-Shape Locked Loop (SSLL) as an Adaptive Separator of Cardiac and Respiratory Components of Bio-Impedance Signal
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: The paper presents an on-line signal processing system for adaptive separation of two infra-low frequency signals: cardiac and respiratory bio-impedance (BI) signals, which are the time varying components of the total BI signal. The separation process of such signals as cardiac and respiratory BI components, is not a trivial filtering due to overlapping of spectra and non stationarity of these signals, and moreover, due to the infra-low frequency range. Therefore, advanced signal processing concepts and methods are needed to achieve the goal. The Signal-Shape Locked Loop (SSLL) concept was introduced to solve the task. Using this concept, it is possible to separate two (or more) independent signal components from the total input signal. Technical solution of the system is intended for applications in portable and implantable cardiac devices.

articleTitle: A Universal Computer Audiometer for Objective Hearing Testing and Screening
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: The authors present the results of a project aimed at constructing and implementing a universal screening audiometer. The construction of the device is based on Pocket PC equipped with external small-size hardware unit containing an amplifier and interface unit, co-operating with an OAE/ABR measuring probe. The system allows for measuring otoacoustic emissions (TEOAE), auditory brainstem responses (ABR), as well as pure-tone audiograms. The audiometer is primarily dedicated to hearing screening of newborns and young children. Due to precision an extended measurement capabilities, it can also be applied to audiological testing and diagnosing hearing disorders in both paediatric and adult patients. The audiometer can be remotely controlled via the Internet and allows access to databases in reference centres, which predestines it to telemedical applications. Preliminary results of application of the instrument in hearing testing are presented. Prospective applications in hearing screening programs are described.

articleTitle: The Dynamic Measurements of Absolute Humidity in Nasal Cavity During Respiration
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: The medicine still requires new, more advanced tools for better human body diagnoses. The great developments in electronics let to construct more and more sophisticated instruments. The system described in the paper lets to check functionality of one of human body subsystems - the breathing system. It can measure dynamic changes of temperature and dew point temperature (absolute value of humidity) of inspired and expired air in different places of human nose and throat. Some example results of dew point hygrometer and temperature measurements during respiration are presented. New factors describing condition and capability of human breathing system are. described.

articleTitle: Implementation of SPR-Biosensors for Express-Diagnostics of Acute Viral Infection and Mycotocsicosis
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: A structure of instrumentation for express-diagnostics of acute viral infection and mycotocsicosis is proposed. It includes an optoelectronic sensor based on surface plasmon resonance and uses artificial neural networks for sensor's signal processing. As result the reliability of diagnostics and resource of developed analytical instrumentation was increased. Using the sensor structures features for saving its parameters allowed to develop the viral-independent measurement transducer.

articleTitle: Multiple Channel Electrooculogram Classification using Automata
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: In this paper, we present a simple and novel technique for classification of multiple channel Electrooculogram signals (EOG). In particular, a viable real-time EOG signal classifier is proposed. The classifier is based on Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA). The system is capable of classifying sixteen different EOG signals and can be used universally for development of hardwired (using VHDL, FPGA etc), or embedded (using Microcontroller etc.) devices requiring EOG as a primary source of input. The viability of the system was tested by performing online experiments with able bodied subjects.

articleTitle: 3D Reconstitution of Dentition by Laser Triangulation Under Structured Lighting
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: The accurate acquisition of the patient dentition is a very important step in orthognathic surgery since it permits to determine the occlusal position in order to prepare the operation. Classical methods for dental acquisition do not give a fast, accurate and low cost solution. Moreover, orthognathic surgery requires accurate registration with CTscan images, which is difficult with state of the art systems, as dental fillings destroy the CT scan images. This paper presents an approach improving simulation and planning techniques by applying the laser triangulation technology in the field of maxillo-facial surgery or dental implants. The originality is found in the combination of the laser scanning technique with a specific double bite wafer and a rigid registration method. The scanner calibration, registration method and tests of impression material are presented, as well as a first validation.

articleTitle: Single Photon Counting System for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: Single photon counting system for biomedical applications was designed and tested. Examination of changes of an optical signal on a patient's head during stimulation tests (finger taping) was made by the elaborated system.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Anemometer for the Measurement of Respiratory Flow in the Forced Oscillation Technique
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: In this paper it is proposed a method to the measurement of respiratory flow in the forced oscillations technique (FOT) using an ultrasonic anemometer. It is used the transit time method and the phase difference technique with the measurements of the phase angle between the signal at the transmission and at the receiver to detect changes in the transit time due to flow. The ultrasonic anemometer implementation is based on a microcontroller. The experimental results of the tests with the comparison among this flowmeter and a classical pneumotachometer used in the FOT for flow measurement will are presented.

articleTitle: Objective Measurement of Pain Intensity by Electrostimulation of Biological Active Points
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: We have established a good correlation between electrical pulse amplitude set by the patient at computerized electroacupuncture stimulation and pain intensity determined according to visual pain scale. Our results show that the value of the pulse amplitude can be used as an objective index of pain intensity before or in the process of pain syndrome treatment.

articleTitle: A Mobile Cytometry Unit Based on Satellite Communications: Cytosat
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: The paper presents a new mobile flow-cytometry device, optimized for diagnostic applications in the oncology field for realizing an integrated remote-diagnosis network based on satellite communications. A prototype of a mobile cytometry unit, presenting the same performances of the traditional flow-cytometers, and remotely controlled thanks to a specific software tool has been designed and developed. Moreover, it is possible to transmit the patient recordings and the analyzed data to a control centre through satellite network. The paper describes both the hardware and the software architecture of the new flow cytometer, focusing, in particular, on the mobility characteristics of the developed instrument.

articleTitle: Evaluation of water barrier function of human skin using super fast dew point hygrometer
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: A new idea of transepidermal water loss factor measurement is presented in the report. Constructed measurement system is base on fast dew point hygrometer with close chamber. For better skin parameterisation, an electrical model of water vapour evaporation through the skin was developed and presented in the paper. Both the experimental results of the dew point hygrometer tests as well as test examination results are shown.

articleTitle: Measurements of Generated Potentials by the Electrodes of a Cochlear Implant
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: In this paper it is described the design and development of an experimental setup to measure in-vitro electric potential distribution delivered by a multichannel cochlear implant varying conditions and parameter of usage. In particular, it was studied the spatial distribution of the electric potential released by this implant. To accomplish this task, an automated process of measurement was built to measure the electric potential inside a tank that resembled the typical environment in which the implant is used in real conditions. This study enables a better comprehension of relationship between parameters of stimulations and the electric potential delivered by the cochlear implant, this is fundamental to develop a more efficient and spatially localized stimulation of the nervous tissues.

articleTitle: Modern Approach to Imaging of Biliary Ducts Stenting
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: A range of minimally invasive interventions is still expanding because the performed procedures may often be more potent and precise than the classical operations. Effectiveness and precision can especially be improved when some combined methods of imaging are used. Videoendoscopy imaging and X-ray imaging are two complementary methods applied during the intervention presented in the paper. These methods facilitate a significant increase in diagnostics and treatment comfort. Interdisciplinary issues of combined medical imaging are presented using some examples of a modern approach to imaging of biliary stenting. The selected examples of effects obtained during interventions assisted by combined imaging of operation site are presented. They have to allow the operator to have great control over the appearance of desirable effects as well as undesirable complications in order to work comfortably and safe.

articleTitle: Technical Performance and Clinical Relevance: Lessons from the GAMUT Study
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: There is an increasing interest in combining information, measurement, and communication technologies into systems for distributed diagnosis and home healthcare. The developer of such systems, however, quickly discovers that technical performance is of little importance by itself, without any reference to clinical relevance. This paper presents some of the lessons learned in the course of a medical device study set to resolve the problem of tuning technical performance (accuracy) to clinical relevance (adequacy) in designing measurement devices for health care purposes.

articleTitle: Autonomous Monitoring of Adverse Responses to Medication - Prolegomena to GAMUT-ARM Trial
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Workshop on Medical Measurement and Applications
abstract: This paper discusses the strategy adopted by a medical device manufacturer to address a basic need in health care: monitoring the patient response to medication. An opening section considers why it is desirable to address this issue technologically, outlining the empirical and rational bases of the manufacturer's project for this. The bulk of the paper reviews the device design modelinspired from aviation safety management and the grounds on which this approach was changed, as an illustration of the clash between metrology and semiology in health care. The final section briefly considers the need of establishing a what is scientific medicine, and what is not, and suggests that autonomous health monitoring is necessary to enable the provision of health care services according to the first principle of medicine.
